items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: I got out of it because I got hold of George Weir to do it and I didn't think I should go down as a producer of a thing like that. I just let him take it all over himself, you know. I did two or three of the concerts, then I got out of it

ctx.x: And so Father Woods had gotten in touch with me to help me. He saw me right away. So I had never been in front of a Bishop and I felt so strange. I just looked at him, you know, with all these colors on and everything. He said, "What can I do for you?" I said, "Jazz, jazz. There won't be any jazz after while." He looked at me and I told him about mother. He had confirmed them and all these people and he loved her, because he has - he does many, many favors for black people.
